source_notes.note: German Tropf means a poor fool or an intravenous drip. Arabic قطرة is not the ordinary lexical equivalent. EN/NL uses the correct German intravenous-drip sense, rather than a generic drop.
kitten is a verb here (mend/cement with putty), although source POS is noun. EN/NL follows the German verb and Arabic meaning.
Wauwau is a children’s word for a dog or its barking, rather than an adjective. EN/NL is labelled as children’s language.
hungern is a verb, although source POS is adjective. EN/NL follows the German verb and Arabic meaning.
keuchen is a verb, although source POS is adjective.
verflixt is a mild swear-word adjective/interjection, although source POS is noun. The mild register is explicit in both meanings.
entsetzen is a verb in this sense, although source POS is adjective.
erstaunen is a verb in this sense, although source POS is adjective.
aufmuntern is a verb, although source POS is noun.
verstreuen is a verb, although source POS is adjective.
zerstreuen is a verb, although source POS is adjective.
weiterfahren is a verb, although source POS is adverb.

source_notes.arabic: عيد القديس مارتن؛ مارتيني مشروب أيضًا
source_notes.note: Martini can name Saint Martin’s Day regionally and the cocktail. Both senses in the Arabic context are retained, rather than silently choosing one.

source_notes.arabic: ورقة الآس في بعض ألعاب الورق؛ لفظ للتعجّب
source_notes.note: Daus is the high card in German-suited decks (historically the deuce, now functioning as the ace). The card-game context and surprise expression are retained.
Nachleben chiefly means continued existence or enduring influence of someone/something. EN/NL avoids religious afterlife so as not to teach the usual false association with Leben nach dem Tod.
